You are implementing wave 1 of the M2 gate-fix round for the SXC-1 Trainer. Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. You own exactly these paths: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/src/SXC1/Exercise/ (Types, Parse, Lint, Verify, Engine, Report) /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/src/SXC1/Route.hs /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/test/CheckExercises.hs /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/app/Main.hs /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/app/View/Exercise.hs /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/content/fixtures/ Do not create or edit anything else. In particular do NOT touch content/exercises/ (the seed content is CLEAN under every rule you are about to add -- I audited it; if your change makes the shipped corpus fail, your change is wrong, not the content), site/src/SXC1/Content/, site/app/View/{Blocks,Pages}.hs, site/static/, or any script. TOOLCHAIN (installed and healthy; do not reinstall, do not change pins) . "$HOME/.ghc-wasm/env" puts wasm32-wasi-ghc / wasm32-wasi-cabal on PATH Host runner for wasm32-wasi COMMAND modules: "$HOME/.ghc-wasm/wasm-run/bin/wasm-run.mjs" [args] Build with -j2. A cold build can exceed a 10-minute foreground timeout -- run it as a BACKGROUND command teed to a log and poll the log. Do not conclude failure from a timeout. Binaries: cd /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site && wasm32-wasi-cabal list-bin exe:exercise-check | tail -1 cd /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site && wasm32-wasi-cabal list-bin exe:content-check | tail -1 The validator reads content off DISK, so a sabotage control is `cp -R` to /tmp, a `sed`, and one run -- no rebuild. Use that; it is why the controls below are cheap enough to be mandatory. STANDING GUARDS -- true before your change and true after, on every task: * the shipped corpus reports 0 issues: exercise-check --content-dir /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/content --translations-dir /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/translations * content-check stays at 357/357 * --fixtures stays green (its count GROWS as new codes gain fixtures; 51 is today's floor) * ALL 32 shipped citation anchors still resolve (the H2 regression guard) * check-site.sh still prints result=complete, and WASM_GZIP_CEILING_BYTES stays 1000000 (app.wasm is ~977 KB gzip against a 1,000,000 ceiling -- roughly 23 KB of headroom for everything you add; measure it and report it, and do NOT raise the ceiling) HOUSE RULE ON CONTROLS: every fix carries a negative control that you demonstrate RED against today's code BEFORE it goes green. A control you only ever saw pass is not a control. Paste both outputs into your report. BACKGROUND YOU MUST NOT REDISCOVER: Codex reviewed read-only and ran nothing; I reproduced every finding at runtime. The reproductions are in briefs/M2-gate-triage.md with exact commands and observed values. Read it first -- it will save you hours. The external adversarial reviewer returned GATE-BLOCKED with sixteen findings. Thirteen are yours. They are grouped below by the file they live in, but they are ONE task because the clock fix must own Engine.hs and Main.hs together, and because every new test lands in the single CheckExercises.hs. ============================================================================= A. THE CLOCK SEAM (H1, H6) -- Engine.hs + Main.hs, and it must not split ============================================================================= Reproduced against the real engine, driving `step` directly: Begin wall0 -> esPromptAt = 1786100000000 (a WALL epoch) Toggle, Submit (mono0 + 8400) -> peElapsed = 0 TRUE 8400 control: Begin mono0, same -> peElapsed = 8400 TRUE 8400 Restart wall0 -> Submit -> peElapsed = 0 TRUE 15000 Main.hs:233 is `Begin . snd <$> readClocks` and readClocks returns (mono, wall), so `snd` is the WALL clock; Main.hs:279 is `Restart wall`. initialState seeds esPromptAt from it and Submit computes `monoMs - esPromptAt` clamped at 0, so every FIRST graded prompt -- and every first prompt after a Restart -- reports a false zero. This is precisely the field M3's spaced repetition will consume. Three more things in the same neighbourhood: * `Advance` never re-baselines esPromptAt (measured: 13400 before, 13400 after), so prompt n+1 is timed from the previous SUBMIT. Time the learner spends reading the explanation before pressing Next is charged to the next prompt. * A cold RExercise route never calls beginIfNeeded (Main.hs:170-181,225-233): state comes from `initialState exid 0`. Be precise about the impact -- I measured it: a cold load, 3 s wait, first answer gives elapsedMs = 3723, which LOOKS right only because Chrome's monotonic origin is page load. It is accidentally correct, not correct, and esStartedAt is wrong. * `Restart` (H7, below) also goes through this path. WHAT TO DO 1. Give Begin and Restart BOTH clocks. Seed esStartedAt and esPromptAt from the MONOTONIC one. 2. Re-baseline esPromptAt on Advance, so each prompt is timed from when it is shown. 3. Issue an initial Begin for a cold exercise route, so a deep-linked exercise starts its clock at display time rather than inheriting the runtime's arbitrary origin. 4. MAKE THE CONFUSION UNREPRESENTABLE, not merely fixed: introduce newtypes `newtype MonoMs = MonoMs Integer` and `newtype WallMs = WallMs Integer`, use them in ExerciseAction and ExerciseState, and thread them from readClocks. After this, `Begin . snd` must not typecheck. This is the point of the fix -- a corrected call site can regress; a type error cannot. CONTROL (must be red first): a --self-test case with deliberately divergent epochs (mono around 5,000; wall around 1,786,100,000,000) that pins peElapsed == 8400 for the FIRST prompt, and a second pinning a real elapsed after Restart. Show them failing against today's engine, then passing. ============================================================================= B. RESTART SHOWS A STALE GRADED SCREEN (H7) -- Main.hs ============================================================================= Reproduced in the browser on q-1-03: after correct submit : feedback "Correct." note? true next? true after RESTART : feedback "Correct." note? true next? true option pressed? false Restart resets ExerciseState but emits no event, so mExResults keeps the previous outcome (Main.hs:241-259,279). The learner gets a fresh, unselected prompt that already tells them they were right, with the explanation and a working Next -- and can complete a "fresh" attempt without answering. Clear this exercise's prompt results on Begin/Restart, or derive displayed feedback from attempt-scoped state. Either is fine; say which you chose and why. ============================================================================= C. DRILL AND LOOKUP CITATIONS ARE NEVER RENDERED (H8) -- View/Exercise.hs ============================================================================= This is the worst finding in the round: it removes the manual-grounding path from two of the three exercise types, and grounding is the milestone's whole premise. Reproduced cold, and again after completion: quiz #ex-cites a.cite = 0 (they DO appear post-answer, via sharedFeedbackEls) drill a.cite = 0 ... and still 0 after all three steps are confirmed lookup a.cite = 0 ... and still 0 after a CORRECT answer The only citation renderer is inside sharedFeedbackEls (View/Exercise.hs:247-266), used only by non-drill bodies; drill sources live in each Prompt's prCites and drillStepsEl never renders them; a lookup's target lives in FindPage and its exCites is normally empty. Render prompt-level citations for drill steps (at/after confirmation) and the FindPage target AFTER GRADING ONLY -- never before, or the lookup spoils its own answer. Keep the existing `` contract and the #ex-cites container so the harness and the CSS keep working. ============================================================================= D. LOOKUP PROSE IS RENDERED TWICE, INSIDE AN INVALID CONTAINER (M6) -- View/Exercise.hs ============================================================================= Reproduced: #ex-stem and #ex-find-task carry identical text, and #ex-find-task contains a block-level child -- a

inside a

, which is invalid HTML. Render the stem once, or make #ex-find-task a div with genuinely distinct content. If you change the element, keep the id. ============================================================================= E. CITATION ANCHORS ARE VACUOUSLY SATISFIABLE (H2) -- Verify.hs ============================================================================= Both defeats reproduced, each reporting 0 issues: cite: guide-book 15 "press the" -- 18 raw chars, 9 normalised: passes the >=12 gate cite: guide-book 10 "|---|---|---|" -- a raw Markdown table delimiter row This defeats the central claim of the citation design. Three changes: 1. measure the >=12 rule on the NORMALISED anchor, not the raw one; 2. match against the RENDERED page text (parsed blocks -> inline text), not the raw Markdown source, so syntax-only anchors cannot match anything; 3. require the normalised anchor to contain at least one letter. I VERIFIED THIS IS SAFE BEFORE MANDATING IT: all 32 shipped anchors -- including the 3 that contain Markdown markers -- still match when both sides are normalised through the same renderer. If your implementation drops any of the 32, normalise both sides the same way rather than relaxing the rule. CONTROL: both defeats above rejected with E-CITE-ANCHOR post-fix, plus the 32/32 audit green. ============================================================================= F. DRILL-STEP TEXT IS EXEMPT FROM THE GLOSSARY (H3) -- Parse.hs + Lint.hs ============================================================================= Reproduced. A two-step drill whose check reads "This machine responds and you should register the sound source" and whose body reads "Press the pad and hit the pad on this machine to register the sound source" -- six violations across four rules -- reports 0 issues. parseStep (Parse.hs:741-785) returns issues/prompt/cites/verifies but NO lint targets. The second half is worse and also reproduced: in a field that IS linted, only the unmarked phrase is caught -- "Do not use the machine plainly. But the **machine** with markup is different." -> exactly ONE E-TERM.term-machine; the marked-up one slips through because inlinesText (Lint.hs:212-223) joins inline nodes with a space, so `the **machine**` becomes `the machine`. Ordinary emphasis defeats the binding glossary in EVERY covered field. Fix both: parseStep must return lint targets for step bodies and `check:` text; and inlinesText must join without inserting separators (or normalise whitespace runs before matching) so rendering-equivalent prose lints identically. CONTROL: the six-violation drill produces an E-TERM finding for every rule it breaks, and `the **machine**` is caught in BOTH a step body and an exercise intro. ============================================================================= G. DECK SLUGS ARE NOT UNIQUE (H4) -- CheckExercises.hs ============================================================================= Reproduced: two indexed decks both declaring `deck: collided-slug`, with distinct valid exercise ids, validate with 0 issues; the report lists the slug twice; #/x/collided-slug resolves to one and the other is unreachable. EXERCISE-FORMAT.md:134 calls it globally unique. Extend globalIdDuplicateIssues to deck slugs, reusing E-ID-DUPLICATE (its detail already names the colliding decks). CONTROL: a dirs/ fixture with two decks sharing a slug. ============================================================================= H. DRILL STEPS MAY HAVE AN EMPTY BODY (H5) -- Parse.hs ============================================================================= Reproduced: a two-step drill whose steps carry only cite: and check: validates with 0 issues and renders confirm buttons with no instructions. EXERCISE-FORMAT.md:175-176 requires at least one block. Emit an issue when stepBodyBlocks is null. CONTROL: a file fixture. ============================================================================= I. CITATION TOTALS MISCOUNT (M1, model half) -- Report.hs ============================================================================= Reproduced on the shipped corpus: 27 `cite:` + 5 `find:` = 32 declarations on disk; the model reports 34. Quiz citations live in both exCites and prCites and count twice; lookup find targets live only in FindPage and count zero. Define `citations` as DECLARATIONS -- one per cite:/find: line -- and count that. Wave 2 rewrites the Python side as a genuinely independent line scan; your job is to make the model's number the one a line scan would produce. CONTROL: assert totals.citations == 32 on the shipped corpus. ============================================================================= J. THE SEAM CAP IS NOT CLOSED OVER EMITTED CODES (M2) -- Report.hs ============================================================================= Report.hs exports `Issue (..)` with `isCode :: !Text`, so any module can construct an issue carrying an arbitrary code without passing through mkIssue/IssueCode. --list-codes derives from allIssueCodes plus the dynamic E-TERM lines, so such a code is invisible to BOTH the coverage invariant and the one-seam cap -- the cap I told the gate to test. Make the dynamic family typed: `IssueCode = ... | E_TERM Text` with `codeText (E_TERM r) = "E-TERM." <> r`, and stop exporting the raw Issue constructor (accessors only; construction via mkIssue). Then every emitted code is enumerable by construction. Keep --list-codes emitting `` and keep the seam class at exactly E-BLOCK-UNPARSED. CONTROL: show that the old raw construction no longer compiles. ============================================================================= K. RENDERED-IDENTICAL CHOICE LABELS (M3) -- Parse.hs ============================================================================= Reproduced: options `A` and `**A**` validate clean and render identically, so the learner faces two visually identical choices. Duplicate detection compares stripped raw Markdown; compare normalised inlinesText instead -- the same normalisation F needs, so land them together. CONTROL: a file fixture with that pair expecting E-CHOICE-DUPLICATE. ============================================================================= L. ROUTES COLLAPSE EMPTY SEGMENTS (L3) -- Route.hs ============================================================================= Reproduced in the browser: #/x//preparation-power/q-1-03 renders the exercise instead of the not-found panel, because nonEmptySegments drops empty components before classification. Reject empty interior segments and validate route ids against [a-z0-9-]+. parseRoute must stay TOTAL and must never call `read`; Int is 32-bit on wasm32, so keep folding page numbers in Integer (that is what M1's NEW8 was about). Do not change M1's existing route spellings or behaviour for well-formed input -- content-check's route group must stay green. CONTROL: self-test cases for "#/x//a/b", "#/x/a//b", "#/x/A B/c" classifying as RNotFound, alongside the existing round-trip and constructor assertions. ============================================================================= M. FIXTURES README DESCRIBES A FIXED DEFECT AS CURRENT (L1) -- content/fixtures/README.md ============================================================================= Line 45 still opens "Known defect this corpus could not route around" and says --fixtures exits non-zero, while the filter it recommends is implemented and the run is 51/51. Rewrite as historical context. Also add fixtures for every new code you introduce -- the coverage invariant will demand them, and --fixtures must stay green. DONE LOOKS LIKE * lib, exe:content-check, exe:exercise-check and exe:app all build -Wall clean. * Every standing guard above holds, and you report the measured app.wasm gzip size. * Every control was demonstrated RED first; both outputs pasted into your report. * Report: what you chose for B (clearing results vs attempt-scoped state) and why; the before/after of the 32-anchor audit; the new fixture count; and the gzip delta.
